--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like strategy with endgame defection and forgiveness when recent cooperation is high. The trace simulates the parent and other population strategies against candidate policies, focusing on mutual cooperation, retaliation, forgiveness, and final-round defection. It considers changing the parent by adding adaptive opponent classification, early exploitation of forgiving strategies, and endgame defection timing.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So, a simple strategy: cooperate until round 99, but if opponent defects, retaliate? Let's design a strategy that: - Cooperates by default. - If opponent defects, we defect next round, then return to cooperation (forgive after one punishment). This is 'forgiving TFT'. - At round 100, always defect."
STRATEGY: The parent is a conditional cooperator with forgiveness and endgame logic; the trace simulates it against a burst of late defections and against always-cooperate-then-defect-last, and revises toward a forgiving TFT with a final-round defection.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says 'Avoid allowing an isolated defection to cause permanent mutual retaliation' and 'Consider forgiveness after a temporary disruption'. But also 'A short punishment followed by renewed cooperation may restore coordination.' So we need to punish to deter exploiters."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-like strategy with forgiveness, exploitation of overly cooperative opponents, and endgame defection. The trace simulates candidate revisions (AC-D100, TFT with final D, double-D trigger, 2-Ds-in-last-3 trigger, stateful double-C reset) against the 12 population slots. It changes the parent by removing early endgame defection and exploitation, and adding a double-defection trigger with forgiveness.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says 'Avoid allowing an isolated defection to cause permanent mutual retaliation.' So we must have a forgiveness mechanism"
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that retaliates on opponent defection, forgives when recent cooperation is high, and defects in the endgame. The trace simulates it against always-D, alternator, slot1 random defector, and other population members. It revises the parent by removing early endgame defection (only defecting at n==99), tightening forgiveness to at most one defection in the last 10, and adjusting exploitation.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So our strategy seems very strong. Even if slot9 gives 245, average ~294."
STRATEGY: Parent defects in the endgame at n>=95 when opponent cooperation is high, plus random exploitation after round 20; the trace simulates the new strategy against parent and other slots; it changes the strategy to forgive a single recent defection, retaliate on repeated defections, and defect only on the last round.
